passages.note: Final-passage (3rd reading) House vote on a single-subject bill; 31 of 94 voting were Nay, so it is not near-unanimous.
passages.actor_quote: Arnold DeVon Mayfield Smith, M Aylesworth Fine McMillin Soliday

passages.provision_quote: A governmental entity may substantially burden a person's exercise of religion only if the governmental entity demonstrates that application of the burden to the person: (1) is in furtherance of a compelling governmental interest; and (2) is the least restrictive means of furthering that compelling governmental interest.
passages.note: Enrolled act text printing the provision Soliday voted for; the only [deleted: ] fences are in the printing-code boilerplate, not in the operative sections.

The bill-details digest is the legislature's description of the instrument and names no act by Soliday (he is not among the authors, co-authors or sponsors), so it fails V1 and V3 and is not in rests_on.

rows.reasoning: Soliday voted Yea on final passage of SB 101 (2015), a single-subject bill adding a new Religious Freedom Restoration chapter whose operative section bars a governmental entity from substantially burdening a person's exercise of religion unless it shows a compelling interest pursued by the least restrictive means. Section 7 extends that defence to individuals and to for-profit entities and section 5 to "any exercise of religion", so the exemption is general rather than tied to one service or field: it matches "protect religious freedom and allow faith-based exemptions from laws that conflict with sincere religious beliefs". It is not "complete autonomy in their operations and hiring practices", because the compelling-interest test limits every exemption and section 11 creates no claim against a private employer.
